Commentary.Commentary: That is it from us then! Zimbabwe almost managed to pull off a draw in this Test but they need not lose heart. They can take confidence from this game and do better in the second Test, which begins on Sunday, 6th November, 2016 at this very same venue. Do join us at 1330 IST (0800 GMT) on the 6th. Until then, Adios! Take Care!

Sri Lanka captain Rangana Herath thinks they did the job in the end but admits the wicket had nothing for the bowlers early on. Says they cannot rely on the weather and they simply had to stick to their plans. Feels it's a new challenge to lead Sri Lanka and at the same time he enjoys his bowling too.

Man of the Match and Zimbabwe captain Graeme Cremer is pleased with the performance as they took the match so far right till the end of day 5 and adds they had a lot of positives in this Test. Admits it was tough as Sri Lanka are a quality side but he's happy to contribute with the runs when his side needed him. Says the wicket was playing around a bit today and it was tough to bat on.

Sri Lanka will be a bit disappointed with their bowling. They struggled in both innings to finish the Zimbabweans off after wrecking the top half. After an ordinary outing in the first innings, debutant Lahiru Kumara did well in the second. Eventually, Herath picked up 6 wickets in the game but Dilruwan did his bit with 5 scalps. Stay tuned for the presentation.

Chasing 412 was never in Zimbabwe's menu and things were looking downcast when they lost 4 wickets for 6 runs in 23 balls. But Williams, Cremer and later Mumba gutsed it out to take it into the last half an hour of the match. Had Cremer not had a brain fade or Mawoyo not been adjudged LBW, we might have possibly seen a draw. Cremer impressed with the ball as well, with a 4-fer in the first innings while Mumba shone in the second, with a 4-wicket haul.

The scorecard will say Zimbabwe lost by 225 runs but what it will not tell is the way they fought. They dropped 5 catches in the first innings, which is why Sri Lanka amassed so much in the first place. With the bat, they did well on the second day in the final session but then lost their way on the third morning. But Cremer, Moor and Tiripano fought hard and helped their side avoid the follow-on.

It was as business as usual for the Lankans with the bat, scoring 537 in the first innings, then reaching almost 250 in the second, setting a target of 412. They would have got more, had it not been for the rain last evening. Apart from Kusal Mendis, everyone played a decent knock in at least one innings.

Heartbreak for Zimbabwe. They fought so hard in this Test, especially the lower order, in both innings, but just fell short in the dying stages. Sri Lanka have won handsomely but Rangana Herath will agree that they could have won it quicker.

There are dark clouds hovering around too and the hosts would be hoping for rain to make its presence felt. Graeme Cremer and Sean Williams are battling out hard and they would look to frustrate the Lankan bowlers. The visitors need to come back hard and pick the remaining wickets quickly else you never know rain might play spoilsport. Join us back in a bit then to catch the final session of this Test match where Zimbabwe are batting against the odds.

That was a good session for Zimbabwe! They just lost one wicket and scored 62 runs in 28 overs. The only batsman who was dismissed was Peter Moor when he got out LBW to the debutant Kumara and in fact he was not out too as the ball tracking technology predicted the ball to be going over the stumps. So Zimbabwe have to survive just one more session but still you would say Sri Lanka are on top since there are just four wickets left.

The players are back out in the middle. PETER MOOR and SEAN WILLIAMS walk out to bat. They still haven't scored a run yet. SURANGA LAKMAL to bowl. Here we go!

Welcome back for the second session. This could possibly be the final one of the match as well. Having lost 4 wickets in quick succession, Zimbabwe are up against it, needing to bat out 64 overs to try and save this Test.
... DAY 5, SESSION 2 ...

So Sri Lanka now need just five wickets in two sessions. The hosts need a miracle to save this Test now. Can the lower order resist enough? Odds are completely against them though. Join us back in a bit for the second session to see how things unfold.

The debutant Kumara struck in his very first over when he bowled a peach of a delivery to dismiss Chari. Mawoyo then was given out LBW to a delivery which would have gone down the leg side and then the hosts collapsed totally. They suddenly lost four wickets in 23 balls as Lakmal and Perera ran through the batting line-up to put Sri Lanka right on top.

That's a terrific end to this session for Sri Lanka! The hosts started off positively as they looked confident in the first hour but the last few minutes went in Sri Lanka's favour completely. Chari and Mawoyo looked gritty in their approach and rightly so as they had to save this Test.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. LUNCH ON DAY 5!

Up went umpire Gould's finger on the appeal. That was crashing onto middle.

Of course, the ball was not hitting the stumps either. Sri Lanka would not mind. End of a stubborn stand and innings.
